target.title: chore: align Android icons with favicon mark
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the Android launcher icon assets still used the older lobster silhouette while the OpenClaw iOS/web mascot uses the newer rounded favicon mark from `ui/public/favicon.svg`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Regenerated all Android launcher PNG density assets from the canonical favicon SVG and switched the adaptive icon background to white so the red favicon mascot remains visible. The adaptive foreground keeps the mascot inside Android's safe zone so launcher masks do not crop the mark.

## User Impact

Android users see the same OpenClaw favicon mascot as the app identity on launcher surfaces instead of the older white lobster silhouette.

AI-assisted: yes, generated with Codex.

## Evidence

- Swept Android launcher/logo references with `rg`; manifest launcher icons, adaptive icon XML, and the foreground service small icon all route through `ic_launcher` / `ic_launcher_foreground`.
- Regenerated `mdpi` through `xxxhdpi` `ic_launcher.png` and `ic_launcher_foreground.png` from `ui/public/favicon.svg`.
- Verified PNG dimensions and alpha channels with `sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight -g hasAlpha`.
- Ran `git diff --check`.
- Attempted `pnpm android:assemble`; first run showed Java was not discoverable, then reran with `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17`. Gradle progressed but this local machine has no Android SDK configured, so it stopped with: `SDK location not found. Define a valid SDK location with an ANDROID_HOME environment variable or by setting the sdk.dir path in apps/android/local.properties`.

Note: `codex --version` fails locally because the installed CLI points at a missing vendor binary (`ENOENT`), so `codex review --base origin/main` could not be run in this environment.

target.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full
target.body:
## Evidence

**Generated 2026-07-07 from the production `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` function on this branch** using `pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts` (not a test runner — calls the exported production seam directly):

```
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts

=== BEFORE: security unset (fail-closed heuristic active) ===
  BLOCKED: cat bad.py | python
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  BLOCKED: bash -c "python bad.py"
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  PASS: python3 script.py | head -30
    (target path `script.py` extractable → no heuristic, file check runs; passes
     because the file does not exist on this machine)

=== AFTER: security="full" (heuristic bypassed) ===
  ALLOWED: cat bad.py | python
  ALLOWED: bash -c "python bad.py"
  ALLOWED: python3 script.py | head -30
```

The `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` seam is exported from the production module (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`). The proof script imports and calls it directly — no vitest, no mocking, no test infra. `BLOCKED` = the function throws; `ALLOWED` = the function returns `undefined`. Before/after behavior confirmed on the same machine in the same Node.js session.

---

## What Problem This Solves

When `exec.security` is `"full"` and `exec.ask` is `"on-miss"` (a common production config), `shouldSkipExecScriptPreflight` returns `false` because it requires `ask === "off"`. This causes `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` to run the fail-closed interpreter heuristic even though the operator has explicitly declared full agent trust.

The heuristic blocks commands that contain an interpreter invocation + complex shell syntax (pipe, `&&`, etc.) when the script target path cannot be extracted — for example `cat bad.py | python`, `bash -c "python script.py"`, or `python <(cat bad.py)`. In lower-trust configurations this defensive fail-close is the right call. At `security="full"` it produces false positives for patterns like `python3 script.py | head -30` where a pipeline prevents target extraction but the intent is unambiguous.

**Root cause**: `ask` controls approval prompts; `security` controls trust level. These were conflated in the outer skip check, which required `ask === "off"` before any preflight could be bypassed at `security="full"`.

## Fix

Thread `security` into `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` and guard the fail-closed interpreter heuristic behind `security !== "full"`. File content validation (shell variable injection detection via `$VAR` patterns) is **unchanged** — it still runs for all security levels whenever a target path can be extracted from the command.

Changes:
- `validateScriptFileForShellBleed`: add optional `security?: ExecSecurity` param; wrap the interpreter heuristic in `if (params.security !== "full")`
- Call site: pass `security` through
- Tests: add `it.each(failClosedCases)` blocks verifying each previously-blocked command now resolves when `security: "full"` is passed, covering both `ask=on-miss` and `ask=always`
- Docs: update `docs/tools/exec.md` to state `security=full` bypasses the heuristic regardless of ask mode

## Test plan

- [x] All existing `failClosedCases` still fail with default (no `security`) param — heuristic unchanged for non-full security
- [x] All existing `passCases` still pass
- [x] New tests verify each `failClosedCase` resolves when `security: "full"` is passed (covers ask=on-miss and ask=always)
- [x] Existing `createPreflightTool()` tests still catch `$VAR` patterns — file content validation runs regardless of security level

Fixes #87371
